**Answer: k = 14**

**Setup.** A rook attacks the nearest piece in each of the four directions. So the condition is that, along every row and every column, any two consecutive pieces (with no piece between them) have opposite colours. Within each line, the pieces must therefore alternate in colour.

**Upper bound.** Let $b_r, w_r$ be the numbers of black and white rooks in row $r$. Alternation means consecutive pieces differ in colour, so $|w_r - b_r| \le 1$, and in particular $w_r - b_r \le 1$. Summing over the 8 rows:

$$k - 6 = \sum_r (w_r - b_r) \le 8,$$

so $k \le 14$.

**Construction with k = 14.** Use coordinates (row, column) with rows and columns numbered 1 to 8.

- Black rooks on the diagonal: $(i,i)$ for $i = 2,\dots,7$ (6 rooks).
- White rooks on the two cells adjacent to the main diagonal: $(k,k+1)$ and $(k+1,k)$ for $k = 1,\dots,7$ (14 rooks).

Check each line:

- Row 1 contains only $(1,2)$; row 8 contains only $(8,7)$.
- Row $i$ for $2 \le i \le 7$ contains $(i,i-1)\,\text{W}$, $(i,i)\,\text{B}$, $(i,i+1)\,\text{W}$, which alternate.
- Column 1 contains only $(2,1)$; column 8 contains only $(7,8)$.
- Column $j$ for $2 \le j \le 7$ contains $(j-1,j)\,\text{W}$, $(j,j)\,\text{B}$, $(j+1,j)\,\text{W}$, which alternate.

In every line the consecutive pieces are opposite in colour, so each rook attacks only rooks of the opposite colour. This gives 14 white rooks with 6 black rooks, matching the bound.

ANSWER: 14
